W7225183140.abstract: Language model agents increasingly act on users' behalf by manipulating external environments through tools, often from high-level instructions that leave critical task- and environment-specific context unstated. To prevent resulting misaligned actions, recent work verifies proposed actions before execution, largely by establishing whether the conditions supporting them hold. We argue that this confirmation-oriented view leaves a fundamental blind spot: a wrong action often passes every check that asks whether it is right. This motivates a different question for verification: rather than asking what evidence supports an action, can the agent find evidence that refutes it? We pursue this direction with BlackSwan, a refutation-oriented, expect-suspect-test procedure that predicts the intended effect of each state-mutating action, formulates specific and empirically testable hypotheses for how it could be wrong, and tests them using existing observations or additional non-mutating actions, executing the action only if none survives testing. On challenging AppWorld tasks, BlackSwan improves success rate over the strongest baseline by 14.9 and 25.2%p with and without the backbone model's thinking mode, respectively. Even without thinking or in-context demonstrations, it outperforms stronger baselines equipped with them. The gains also transfer beyond AppWorld, with BlackSwan improving WebShop performance by 12.7%p. More broadly, our results suggest that language model agents have an underused capacity to recognize and self-correct misaligned actions, which can be systematically elicited through active conjecture and refutation before execution.

W7225237945.abstract: Cancer immunotherapy has revolutionized oncology by harnessing the immune system to recognize and eliminate malignant cells. Despite remarkable clinical successes, a substantial proportion of patients fail to respond or develop resistance, highlighting the urgent need for reliable biomarkers to guide patient selection, predict therapeutic outcomes, and monitor treatment responses. This review addresses both the emerging and established biomarkers for cancer immunotherapy. These include molecular, cellular, and systemic biomarkers within tumor tissues, blood, and the tumor microenvironment. The principal ones include immune checkpoint-related biomarkers (e.g., programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression), tumor mutational burden, microsatellite instability, neoantigen profiling, circulating tumor DNA, and immune cell signatures. We grade each biomarker by analytical validity, clinical validity, clinical utility and regulatory readiness; place it in one of four evidence tiers; and outline the steps needed to bring candidate markers into the clinic. Recent developments in multi-omics technologies, artificial intelligence, and single-cell analysis are accelerating biomarker discovery, providing a clearer understanding of tumor–immune interactions. Furthermore, the integration of dynamic biomarkers is critical for optimally refining therapeutic strategies for real-time monitoring and detection of resistance mechanisms. This review aims to provide a worldwide overview of present achievements, challenges, and future opportunities in biomarker research and ultimately enable the development of more personalized and effective strategies for immunotherapy of cancer.

W7225376287.abstract: To address the problems of insufficient adaptability of fixed processes, failure cascading, and uncontrolled resource consumption in long-chain tasks for large language model agents, this paper proposes a state-aware adaptive orchestration mechanism based on dynamic task graphs and budget constraints.This mechanism combines task difficulty, execution history, remaining budget, quality confidence and risk exposure into a single state vector, and then selects a workflow based on the combined utility of quality, cost, latency and risk.Runtime re-orchestration is performed by online reliability updates, partial rollbacks and verification gates.Secondary statistics from publicly available data on WebArena and automated agent design research show that the overall success rate of fixed agents in real-world long-chain environments is significantly lower than that of manual operations.Workflows obtained through automated search also outperform representative manual processes in the four task categories of reading, mathematics, multi-task and science.This study shows that the orchestration object should change from a fixed role sequence to an observable, evaluable and rollback-capable dynamic task graph, and provides a way to build stable and cost-effective agent systems.

W7225417722.abstract: For the developing 6G communication framework to transform next-generation communications utilizing distributed networking paradigms (Multi-Agent Systems or MAS) with advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) capabilities, large Language Models (LLM) will serve as intelligent coordinators that empower autonomous agents (i.e., user equipment, network nodes, edge devices) with natural language understanding and reasoning capability. This allows these agents to negotiate, cooperate and make real-time decisions, enabling ultra-reliable, low-latency and high-capacity communications, which are key requirements for 6G applications such as smart cities, immersive extended reality (XR) experiences, and autonomous transportation. By using LLMs as the basis for context-aware, semantic information exchange between agents, LLMs enhance spectrum efficiency, support adaptive resource allocation, and enable interference management using intelligent, intent-based communication protocols. In addition, LLMs automate the configuration of, fault diagnosis of, and detection of security threats within a distributed agent environment, thus being integral to the zero-touch network management capability within 6G networks. MAS provide a federated approach that significantly enhances robustness and scalability, allowing the communication network to self-organize and adaptively optimize its performance in highly dynamic operating environments. Therefore, the paradigm of using LLM-enhanced MAS represents the next radical step toward creating human-centric, intelligent, and autonomous 6G communication networks able to support the unprecedented complexity and diverse needs of connected societies in the future.
